prompt: Which is the better title for a ticket?
hint: A title that decides the answer skips the question.

choices.text: Add a paragraph to index.html
choices.why: That is a solution, chosen before anybody looked at the problem.

choices.text: Holidays are missing from the site
choices.why: Right. It says what is wrong and leaves the how open.

choices.text: Urgent!!
choices.why: It says how somebody felt, and nothing about the work.

choices.text: Bruno's request from the September meeting
choices.why: Nobody can tell what it is about without finding the meeting.

prompt: The ticket ends: Done when: the home page says we close on public holidays. What is that line for?
hint: Who decides when it is finished?

choices.text: It is the commit message Ana must use
choices.why: Commit messages describe commits; this describes the outcome.

choices.text: It sets a deadline for the work
choices.why: There is no date in it; it describes a result.

choices.text: It says how everybody will know it is finished
choices.why: Right. Those are acceptance criteria.

choices.text: It lists the files to change
choices.why: It names a page as the reader sees it, not a file.

prompt: Why does the ticket's number go into the branch name and the commits?
hint: Think of somebody running git blame a year later.

choices.text: Git refuses a branch without one
choices.why: Git knows nothing of tickets; the number is a habit.

choices.text: It makes the commits sort in order
choices.why: Commits are ordered by their parents, not their messages.

choices.text: It hides the branch from other people
choices.why: A name hides nothing.

choices.text: So the code leads back to its reason
choices.why: Right. blame finds the commit, the commit names the ticket.

prompt: Ana picks up ticket 23. What does she do on the board before writing code? Choose all that apply.
hint: Two things, both so other people know.

choices.text: Assigns it to herself
choices.why: Yes. Nobody else starts the same work.

choices.text: Moves it to in progress
choices.why: Yes. The board then shows what is being worked on.

choices.text: Closes it, since she is taking it
choices.why: It closes when the change is merged.

choices.text: Rewrites its title as the fix
choices.why: The title stays the problem.

prompt: Why does Ana run git pull on main before creating the branch?
hint: Somebody else merged yesterday.

choices.text: To start from today's main
choices.why: Right. A stale start turns into avoidable conflicts.

choices.text: Because git switch -c needs a network
choices.why: Creating a branch is purely local.

choices.text: To send her work to the server
choices.why: pull brings work in; push sends it out.

choices.text: To delete old branches on the server
choices.why: pull deletes nothing.

prompt: git switch main says Your branch is up to date with 'origin/main', and the next git pull brings in a commit. How can both be true?
hint: When did Git last ask the server?

choices.text: The pull made a new commit of its own
choices.why: It was a fast-forward to Bruno's merge; no commit was made.

choices.text: The first message compares with the last fetch
choices.why: Right. origin/main was stale until pull fetched.

choices.text: The server was down during the switch
choices.why: switch never contacts the server.

choices.text: Git's message is simply wrong
choices.why: It is accurate about what Git knew then.

prompt: On the branch 23-holiday-notice, what does git log --oneline main.. list?
hint: Read main.. as from main to here.

choices.text: Every commit in the repository
choices.why: The range excludes everything main already has.

choices.text: The commits on main made since the branch started
choices.why: That is ..main, the other direction.

choices.text: Commits here that main lacks
choices.why: Right. What the pull request will contain.

choices.text: Only merge commits
choices.why: It lists ordinary commits; there are no merges on the branch.

prompt: A pull request's description reads ___ #23, and merging it shuts ticket 23 by itself.
hint: A keyword the hosting service reads; Refs only links.

prompt: Match each piece of text to what it does.
hint: One description matches nothing.

pairs.right: The branch the work is on

prompt: What belongs in the pull request's description? Choose all that apply.
hint: What does a reviewer need before reading the diff?

choices.text: Closes #23
choices.why: Yes. It links and closes the ticket.

choices.text: How to check the change
choices.why: Yes. The reviewer can see it work.

choices.text: The whole diff, pasted in
choices.why: The diff is already on the page.

choices.text: What it changes, in a sentence or two
choices.why: Yes. It orients the reader.

choices.text: Every command Ana ran
choices.why: Nobody reviews the commands; they review the result.

prompt: When is a draft pull request the right choice?
hint: It can be read but not merged.

choices.text: When the change should never be merged
choices.why: Then it needs no pull request at all.

choices.text: When you want comments before it is finished
choices.why: Right. It runs the checks and cannot be merged by mistake.

choices.text: When the branch has only one commit
choices.why: The number of commits does not matter.

choices.text: When nobody is available to review
choices.why: A draft still waits for a reviewer.

prompt: Bruno asks for the notice to stand out more. What does Ana do?
hint: The pull request follows its branch.

choices.text: Closes it and opens a new pull request
choices.why: The conversation would be split across two pages.

choices.text: Commits on the same branch and pushes
choices.why: Right. The pull request updates by itself.

choices.text: Edits the file on main directly
choices.why: That skips the review Bruno is doing.

choices.text: Asks Bruno to make the change himself
choices.why: The author answers the review; lesson 14.

prompt: The pull request was merged on the website. What does Ana's local main need?
hint: The merge happened on the server.

choices.text: Nothing; it updates itself
choices.why: Nothing on the laptop changes until Git asks.

choices.text: A git push
choices.why: There is nothing new to send.

choices.text: A git pull
choices.why: Right. It brings in the merge commit.

choices.text: A new clone
choices.why: pull is enough.

prompt: Why does git branch -d 23-holiday-notice succeed after the pull?
hint: Lesson 5 showed when it refuses.

choices.text: Branches are deleted after a week
choices.why: Git never deletes a branch on its own.

choices.text: Its commits are in main now
choices.why: Right. Nothing would be lost.

choices.text: The server deleted it first
choices.why: The local branch is separate from the one on the server.

choices.text: -d deletes whatever it is given
choices.why: That is -D; -d refuses unmerged work.

prompt: What does git log --oneline --no-merges v1.0..v1.1 give the team?
hint: Read the range and the flag separately.

choices.text: The commits made on the day of v1.1
choices.why: The range is about tags, not dates.

choices.text: Every merge between the two releases
choices.why: --no-merges leaves the merges out.

choices.text: The difference between two files
choices.why: log lists commits; diff shows lines.

choices.text: The raw material for release notes
choices.why: Right. What v1.1 has that v1.0 did not.

prompt: git tag --contains 0b46e2a prints v1.1. What does that tell Ana?
hint: It answers which release, not whether it is running.

choices.text: v1.1 was made from that commit alone
choices.why: v1.1 contains three changes; the commit is one of them.

choices.text: The commit is part of v1.1
choices.why: Right. If v1.1 is running, so is the change.

choices.text: The commit is not merged yet
choices.why: A tag on main containing it means it was merged.

choices.text: The customers can see it now
choices.why: Only if v1.1 is what is deployed.

prompt: Ticket 23 closed when the pull request merged. Is the task done?
hint: Can a customer see the notice yet?

choices.text: Yes; closed means done
choices.why: The change is merged, not released.

choices.text: Yes, once Bruno approved
choices.why: An approval is a step before the merge.

choices.text: Not until a customer confirms it
choices.why: Somebody on the team checks it; no customer is asked.

choices.text: Not until it is released and checked
choices.why: Right. Lesson 17 calls that the definition of done.

prompt: Put the life of ticket 23 in order.
hint: The number goes into the branch before any commit exists.
items: She commits with Refs #23 and pushes
She opens a pull request saying Closes #23
Bruno approves and it is merged
trap: Tagging before the merge releases a version without the change.

prompt: After the merge on the website, put Ana's commands in order.
hint: Delete only what main already has.
trap: Deleting before the pull makes -d refuse: local main does not have the commits yet.

prompt: On 23-holiday-notice, Ana spots a wrong price on the menu page. What should she do with it?
hint: One ticket, one branch, one pull request.

choices.text: Fix it in this branch, since she is there
choices.why: Then a holiday review carries a price change nobody asked about.

choices.text: Leave it; it is not her ticket
choices.why: Somebody who saw it should make sure it is written down.

choices.text: Write a ticket for it
choices.why: Right. It gets its own branch and review.

choices.text: Mention it in the commit message
choices.why: Nobody reads commit messages as a to-do list.

prompt: Which of these are true? Choose all that apply.
hint: Two are things Git does not know about.

choices.text: Git closes a ticket when a commit says Closes
choices.why: The hosting service does; Git has no tickets.

choices.text: Tickets and pull requests share one counter on GitHub
choices.why: Yes. That is why the pull request is #24.

choices.text: A tag marks exactly what went out in a release
choices.why: Yes. Lesson 7.

choices.text: Merged and released are the same moment everywhere
choices.why: Only where every merge is deployed automatically.
